title: Rectangular base
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, initiate a two-dimensional sketch and draw a single loop consisting of four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0). The second line extends from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0131). The third line goes from (0.75, 0.0131) to (0.0, 0.0131), and the fourth line completes the rectangle by connecting (0.0, 0.0131) back to the origin. Apply a sketch scale of 0.75 to the drawn rectangle. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the scaled and transformed sketch along its normal by 0.0131 units and in the opposite direction by 0.0 units to create a solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular base are 0.7499999700000163 units in length, 0.013124992912503812 units in width, and 0.013124993332503599 units in height.

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch on the XY plane
sketch = (
    workplane
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.0)  # line_1
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.0131)  # line_2
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0131)  # line_3
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0)  # line_4
    .close()  # Close the loop
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.0131)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0131, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0131, 0.0131) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0131) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
